summary: A change notice for IMP system version 2514, scheduled for installation in January 1972. It fixes problems with the delay applied after a host comes up, backing it off to 30 seconds and removing an ambiguity that could make it far longer.

plainLanguage.summary: This notice describes a change in IMP software version 2514. It sets a clear 30-second delay before accepting more than one packet from a host, while requiring the host to receive network messages immediately.

questions: what is the imp delay when a host comes online
why did version 2514 change the host delay
what must a host do when coming alive on the network
what was the imp startup delay in version 2514
subtitle: A notice about the IMP 2514 update and its host startup delay.

tldr.problem: IMP version 2513 introduced a long and ambiguous delay before accepting a second packet from a host coming alive.
tldr.mechanism: Version 2514 reduces the delay to 30 seconds and removes the ambiguity described in the notice.
tldr.outcome: Hosts must be ready to accept network messages as soon as they indicate they are alive, even during the delay.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 271 as Unknown and records no RFC that updates or obsoletes it. The RFC is an operational change notice for IMP software.

sections.title: The IMP Version Update
sections.content:
The note announces planned installation of IMP system version 2514 on January 13, 1972, between noon and 1 p.m. Eastern time. The installation requires assistance from IMP-site personnel.

The update addresses two problems associated with version 2513 and the delay after a host indicates it is coming alive.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN planned to install IMP version 2514 on January 13. The update addresses problems with the wait applied when a host comes back online.

sections.title: The Delay in Version 2513
sections.content:
Version 2513 lengthened the delay to slightly more than 40 seconds, causing hardware difficulties for some hosts. An ambiguity could also make the delay last as long as a minute and a quarter.

Version 2514 backs the delay off to 30 seconds and removes the ambiguity. The notice says BBN Report 1822 specified that the delay may range from 30 to 90 seconds and future versions may require longer delays.
sections.plainLanguage: The previous wait was longer than 40 seconds and could stretch to a minute and a quarter. Version 2514 sets the wait at 30 seconds and removes the ambiguity.

sections.title: What a Host Must Do
sections.content:
A host indicates it is coming alive either by sending something to the IMP after a voluntary shutdown or by raising its ready line after an involuntary shutdown. In either case, the IMP refuses to accept more than one packet from the host for 30 seconds.

The host must nevertheless accept all messages from the network as soon as it indicates it is alive. The notice explains that failing to do so may cause the IMP's ready line to drop briefly during the delay.
sections.plainLanguage: The IMP waits before accepting more packets from a returning host. The host still has to accept incoming network messages right away.

references.text: RFC 270, cited for the IMP Ready Line behavior.
